_meta.contract: Every entry names its source creature. template_2014 present when that creature exists in both SRDs.

damage_slots.rider: {rider_damage} ... — ADDITIVE second instance ("plus 4 (1d8) Acid damage"). Sums with the main damage.
damage_slots.alternative: {alt_damage} ... — an ALTERNATIVE that REPLACES the main damage under a condition ("or 12 (2d8+3) Piercing damage if the target is Grappled", or a swarm's reduced damage while Bloodied). Never sum it with the main damage.
damage_slots.budget_split: Across the 136 purely additive multi-damage attacks in the SRD the main instance carries a median 61% of the attack total (quartiles 50/61/71). Split a per-attack budget roughly 60/40 main to rider.
damage_slots.why: Every one of these 157 rows previously reused the SAME {damage} slot for both instances, so substituting one value rendered the rider at full main-damage value. The Ancient Red Dragon's Rend would have read 38 instead of 29, about 31% hot. Verified by round-tripping all 162 slotted rows against the printed SRD text.
damage_slots.self_damage: Rows tagged self_damage (the two Vampire Weakness entries) keep literal numbers: they are damage the creature takes from sunlight or running water, not output, so an attack budget does not apply.
damage_slots.flat_damage_source: Rows tagged flat_damage_source came from a creature whose attack deals flat damage with no dice (the CR 0 animals: Bat, Cat, Rat). They now carry slots so they can scale.

reach.rule: follows creature SIZE, not CR. Holding size at Medium, reach stays 5 ft across every CR band; varying size gives 5/5/5/10/15.

target_size.rule: a "Medium or smaller" gate lands on the creature's OWN size half the time and one step smaller 31% of the time; median offset is 0. Default to the creature's size.

area.rule: Cone follows CR on the dragon-breath ladder (wyrmling 15, young 30, adult 60, ancient 90, Tarrasque 150). Combat Emanations follow CR weakly. Emanations above 60 ft are audible-range control effects and are pinned, not scaled.
area._note: Every value is a multiple of 5 feet: D&D areas always are. Cone follows the dragon-breath ladder. Lines follow the same ladder one step behind. Emanations above 60 ft are audible-range effects and are pinned instead (the Harpy has a 300-foot Luring Song at CR 1).

push_distance.rule: scales with CR: the Bronze Dragon line runs 30/40/60/60 from wyrmling to ancient.

sight_range.rule: targeting range scales with CR (30/90/120/120). Sensory ranges above 200 ft are pinned, like the emanations.

teleport_distance.rule: thin sample; held at the observed band median.

_meta.slot_type: Assigned with the SAME classifier that produced composition.by_band, so the picker filters on exactly what was counted. A mismatch here would silently make the sampled counts unfillable.

damage_ratios.area_vs_round: An area effect deals about ONE FULL ROUND of attacks, not half: median 1.01x across the 64 SRD creatures having both (Ancient Red 91 vs 87, Adult Red 59 vs 54, Wyrmling 24 vs 24). Split by gating, a gated area is 1.03x and an ungated one 0.30x — the recharge gate is what pays for full-round damage in an area. Halving area damage unconditionally, as the old chassis did, left them ~50% weak.

_meta.flavor_slots: {substance} and {delivery} are FLAVOR, filled by the model, never by the engine — exactly like {creature} and the ability name. A template that says "exhales lightning" forces every creature built from it to have lungs and a lightning theme; the mechanics (save, DC, area, damage, counterplay) are the reusable part, and the element is not. {damage_type} was already a slot, so this closes the same hole in the surrounding prose.
_meta.flavor_slots_extra: {kindred_type} is the generated creature's OWN type. The mechanic "my aura does not harm my own kind" is generic; the Lich naming Undead is flavor. A fiendish creature built from that template spares fiends instead. Note the OTHER type references are NOT flavor: a Wight raising a slain Humanoid as a zombie, or lycanthropy infecting a Humanoid, is about the victim being a person and is correct for any creature carrying the ability.
_meta.signature: An ability printed on exactly ONE creature. It is not excluded — a lich's Disrupt Life on some other monster is a good outcome — but it needs a harder reskin than a Bite does, because a reader who knows the SRD will recognise it. Rarity is already handled without a rule: the pool keeps duplicate rows, so weighted picking is proportional to how many creatures share a mechanic. A one-off draws around 1% per slot while the common breath template draws 18%. `sources_sharing` carries that count on every row.
_meta.archetypes: Overlapping affinity tags derived from an ability MECHANICS, not from its source creature: a Constrictor's Constrict is both brute and controller, a Giant Spider's Web is controller and lurker. Derived from the required_slots each archetype declares in archetype-chassis-spec.json — brute wants heavy melee, artillery a 60ft+ ranged attack or a zone, controller a save that imposes a condition, lurker concealment or a gated nova, skirmisher a movement trick, support something that targets allies, defender a reaction. Used as a WEIGHT and never a filter (x3 on a match, x0.5 on a miss, x1 for untagged): asking for a lurker makes lurker mechanics likelier without ever excluding a breath weapon. The archetype itself comes from the existing resolve micro-call, so a user concept reaches ability selection with no extra LLM round. The old archetype system CONSTRAINED the slot plan, which is part of why every monster of a role felt alike.
_meta.damage_class: How an entry's damage is BUDGETED, stamped offline: attack (one attack's worth), area (a round's worth when gated, 0.3x ungated), save_nuke (0.3x a round), legendary (0.55x one attack — printed legendary uses run 7-17), recurring (0.5x one attack — printed auras run half an attack, Balor 13 at CR 19). slot_type is a SAMPLING category and was doing double duty as the damage category, which is how a legendary entry with area text bypassed area budgeting and shipped a 31-damage breath.
_meta.facets: Theme facets on two axes — BODY (bestial, armed, amorphous) and DOMAIN (grave, fiendish, celestial, fey, draconic, elemental, verdant, forged, mind, venomous, terror, beguiling, grasping, devouring, aquatic, subterranean, aerial, uncanny, arcane, voice, gaze, breath) — derived deterministically from what flavor-stripping could not remove: source type, condition economy, delivery mechanics, name keywords. The resolve call picks 2-3 for the concept; the picker weights abilities, traits, packages and menus by overlap. Guide, never constraint: untagged rows stay neutral, mismatches are damped, nothing is excluded. This is the anti-theme-soup layer (owner call, 2026-08-02): the Skreek was simultaneously swamp, frost, rift and bone because selection had no theme signal at all.
_meta.generification_stop_words: Sweeps that replace source-name words with {creature} MUST skip rules vocabulary: Invisible (the Invisible Stalker is named after its condition and lost "has the Invisible condition" to the sweep TWICE — the flavor-free guard test now catches it). Conditions, senses, and sizes are never name-leak candidates.

spell_policy._note: Measured off every printed spellcasting monster. The split that matters is FUNCTION, not raw level: at-will OFFENSIVE spells cap at level 2 in print (Scorching Ray, Mind Spike, Invisibility), while self-utility runs to level 9 at will (metallic dragons carry Shapechange). Level 3+ offense belongs in the 1/Day list. A naive "level 4+ never at will" rule would flag half the printed dragons; a missing rule shipped at-will Hold Monster on a live block.

condition_slots._doc: Owner-directed generification (2026-08-03): condition riders become engine-filled slots so a concept can color its control by severity tier. Measured from the 243 printed condition clauses in this library: save stat correlates hard with condition (Frightened is Wis 12/13, Poisoned Con 13/13, the whole hard tier Con), severity lives in the row's gate and duration clause (so the TIER is named in the slot, fixed per row), and printed pairs are curated, never composed. The ENGINE fills these at build time, seeded, weighted toward the row's printed original (condition_default x4) and the block's theme affinities (x3) — guide, never constrain. The flavor model is never asked: conditions are mechanics. Structural conditions stay literal: Grappled/Restrained (escape-DC machinery), Prone (charge/knockdown), Petrified (two-failure ladder), Unconscious (wake clause), Incapacitated singles (nova-classed, mixed saves).

composition._note: Per-slot count distributions, sampled INDEPENDENTLY. Draw each slot's count from its own `weights` map (key = count, value = how many SRD creatures had exactly that count), then fill each slot from any library entry. Do not sample joint shapes: at CR 8-14 there are 37 distinct shapes across 41 creatures and 33 of them occur exactly once, so the most common joint shape describes 4% of monsters. Sampling joint shapes reproduces one creature's skeleton, which is the failure the hand-built template library had.

_slot_types.plain_attack: attack roll, damage only. Flat ~1 at EVERY CR: Multiattack multiplies it, so this is not a CR axis.
_slot_types.rider_attack: attack roll that also imposes a condition. Also flat (~0.3) at every CR.
_slot_types.area: cone, line, emanation, cube, sphere or radius.
_slot_types.save_effect: saving throw imposing a condition, no attack roll.
_slot_types.utility: no attack, no save: Spellcasting, teleports, healing.
_slot_types.trait: passive. The main growth axis: 0.67 at CR 0-2 rising to ~2.1 at CR 15+.
_slot_types.legendary: legendary actions. Zero below CR 8, 2.75 at CR 21-30.
_slot_types.gated: count of entries carrying Recharge / per-Day / once-per-turn. A cross-cutting count, not a separate slot.

composition._dragon_skew: 8 of 12 creatures at CR 21-30 and 9 of 17 at CR 15-20 are dragons, and they share one layout: one attack, one breath-shaped area, three legendary actions. Sampling the high bands as printed makes every high-CR monster dragon-shaped (area mean 0.72 with dragons, 0.25 without). So the VARIETY slots at CR 15+ pool the band with the CR 8-14 non-dragons, while the COMPLEXITY slots (trait, legendary, gated) come from the band alone: those are genuinely CR-driven, and pooling them collapsed legendary from 2.14 to 1.13 when every CR 21-30 creature has legendary actions. Each slot records which population it came from in `sampled_from`.
composition._beasts: the 89 Beasts are excluded throughout; they skew the low bands to "one attack and nothing else".

multiattack._note: How many attacks the Multiattack line grants. Profiling skipped these lines because they are not ability slots, but the count is load-bearing: per-attack damage from cr-table times this count is the creature's routine round. Attack ENTRY count stays flat at ~1 across all CRs; this is what scales.

size._note: Creature size by CR band, observed. The engine picks size BEFORE the flavor call because reach and the hit-die face both follow it — a Gargantuan creature has 15 ft. reach and d20 hit dice. The model is told the size rather than asked for one.

packages._note: Synergy packages: abilities within ONE creature that reference each other, feed each other's conditions (imposes->requires), or share a form gate. Mined deterministically; every member is a library row and rescales through the same machinery as any single pick. A package is the coherence unit the hand-built v1 library had and slot sampling lost: the members were DESIGNED together. Packages cross trait/action/legendary lines on purpose (owner call): traits are tied to actions, and a package that cannot cross sections cannot carry the tie.

on_death._note: The after-death slot (owner design, 2026-08-02). Four families: continuity (reforms — in a place, at an anchor, from a trophy), succession (something inherits), residue (the death leaves a persistent thing), conditional (permanence has a condition players can pursue). Selection derives from what the block already knows: creature type gives the default family, themes pick specifics. Optional, ramped toward the top of the CR range — on-death lore on a CR 3 is noise; on a CR 20 it is the difference between a boss and a set piece. Two sentences maximum (the ghost-possession lesson). PORTABILITY RULE: effects point at canonical planes or at the creature's own material ("its hoard", "its oldest bargain") — never invented geography ("the Cinder Waste" reads tacked on).
